definition: A linguistic minority is a group seen as being in the minority because of the language its members speak. In this context, perceiving one’s group as a linguistic minority can shape social identity and is linked to possible negative effects on well-being and community participation.

reasons: The definition’s first sentence provides an explicit definitional characterization (“a group seen as being in the minority because of the language its members speak”), but the packet only refers to “perceiving one’s own group as a linguistic minority” and does not define what qualifies as a linguistic minority.

The packet does not define the term in general; it only discusses Basque speakers and the effect of perceiving one’s own group as a minority, so the first-sentence gloss is not directly supported as a dictionary definition.

The claim that perceiving one’s group as a linguistic minority "can shape social identity" goes beyond the packet, which says social identification is associated with well-being and community participation and may offset negative effects, not that minority perception itself shapes identity.
